recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce xpathUsage or duplicate explanatory metadata for FHIR-3341; any remaining legacy XPath cleanup belongs to the later FHIR-32530/FHIR-35974 issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-3341 was a Published/Not Persuasive FHIR-I change request asking for model-driven metadata to distinguish normal path-based search parameters from resource-specific algorithms, citing DSTU1 examples such as ImagingStudy size, Location near/nearDistance, Patient/RelatedPerson/Organization phonetic, and SecurityEvent patientId. Its resolution said this had been done by another tracker using paths and xpathUsage.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-3341 was found. The matching application was FHIR-3317, which added SearchParameter.xpathUsage in commit 572c59da417c5781bef6e10f35c9ba05d2113b40; current source carries the successor SearchParameter.expression and SearchParameter.processingMode representation.
additional_context: FHIR-32530 later removed SearchParameter.xpath and renamed xpathUsage to processingMode, and FHIR-35974 trimmed obsolete mode codes while retaining other. FHIR-I Zulip and Confluence evidence confirms those were intentional later decisions. fhir.ini lists the relevant resources and SearchParameter as active and maps the old xpathUsage name to processingMode for version conversion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current resource search parameter bundles include expressions and processingMode values; Location near is marked other, the phonetic parameters are marked phonetic, and obsolete candidate codes such as ImagingStudy size, Location nearDistance, and AuditEvent patientId are not current search parameters.

related_jiras.note: This Published tracker added xpathUsage for missing phonetic path metadata and appears to be the 'another tracker' cited by FHIR-3341.
